title: Topic, headers and unroutable messages
summary: Write the topic matcher, route on headers, and stop losing messages that match no binding: mandatory, basic.return and alternate exchanges.

steps.title: How a topic match works
body: Split the binding pattern and the routing key on `.` and walk both word lists:
- a plain word must equal the key's word;
- `*` consumes **exactly one** word;
- `#` consumes **zero or more** words, so try both "skip it" and "eat one more word".
The match succeeds when both lists run out together. Step through `order.#.created` against
`order.eu.created` and watch the recursion try `#` = nothing first, then `#` = `eu`.
> **See it:** **Labs → Messaging builder → RabbitMQ**, challenge *The wildcard that never matches*.

code: bool Match(string[] p, int i, string[] k, int j)
return Match(p, i + 1, k, j) || (j < k.Length && Match(p, i, k, j + 1));
return j < k.Length && (p[i] == "*" || p[i] == k[j]) && Match(p, i + 1, k, j + 1);

return Match(p, i + 1, k, j) || (j < k.Length && Match(p, i, k, j + 1));
return j < k.Length && (p[i] == "*" || p[i] == k[j]) && Match(p, i + 1, k, j + 1);
steps.explain: `#` may match zero words, so `order.created` matches. The pattern must also end where the key ends, so the trailing `v2` has nothing left to match it.

steps.prompt: Which routing keys does the binding `order.#.created` match? Select all that apply.
steps.explain: The first word must be exactly `order` (not `orders`), the last exactly `created`, and `#` takes whatever lies between, including nothing.

steps.title: A topic-exchange matcher
prompt: Write `bool TopicMatches(string pattern, string routingKey)` with RabbitMQ's topic rules:
- words are separated by `.`;
- `*` matches **exactly one** word;
- `#` matches **zero or more** words;
- any other word must be equal (case-sensitive).
```text
TopicMatches("order.*.created", "order.eu.created")  → true
TopicMatches("order.*.created", "order.created")     → false
TopicMatches("order.#", "order")                     → true
solution: static bool Match(string[] p, int i, string[] k, int j)
return Match(p, i + 1, k, j) || (j < k.Length && Match(p, i, k, j + 1));
return j < k.Length && (p[i] == "*" || p[i] == k[j]) && Match(p, i + 1, k, j + 1);
hints: Split both on `.` and write a recursive helper `Match(p, i, k, j)` over word positions.
For `#`: `Match(p, i + 1, k, j) || (j < k.Length && Match(p, i, k, j + 1))`.
template: Dojo.Eq("order.created does not match order.*.created", false, TopicMatches("order.*.created", "order.created"));
Dojo.Eq("order.eu.b2b.created does not match order.*.created", false, TopicMatches("order.*.created", "order.eu.b2b.created"));
Dojo.Eq("order matches order.# (zero words)", true, TopicMatches("order.#", "order"));
Dojo.Eq("order.us does not match order.eu", false, TopicMatches("order.eu", "order.us"));
Dojo.Eq("order.eu.created does not match order.*", false, TopicMatches("order.*", "order.eu.created"));
Dojo.Eq("orders.eu.created does not match order.#", false, TopicMatches("order.#", "orders.eu.created"));

steps.title: Headers exchanges
body: A headers exchange ignores the routing key and matches the **binding arguments** against the message
**headers**. `x-match` decides how: `all` (every listed header must be equal) or `any` (at least one).
```csharp
await channel.ExchangeDeclareAsync("documents", ExchangeType.Headers, durable: true);
await channel.QueueBindAsync("print-a4", "documents", routingKey: "",
arguments: new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["x-match"] = "all", ["format"] = "pdf", ["paper"] = "a4" });
var props = new BasicProperties
Headers = new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["format"] = "pdf", ["paper"] = "letter" },
Arguments starting with `x-` are not compared (`all-with-x` / `any-with-x` include them). Headers exchanges are
slower and harder to see in tooling than topics; reach for them only when the routing really depends on
several independent attributes.
> **See it:** **Labs → Messaging builder → RabbitMQ**, challenge *Route on headers*.

steps.prompt: A message with headers `format=pdf, paper=letter` is published to the `documents` headers exchange. Which queues receive it? Select all that apply.
steps.explain: `all` needs every listed header equal (`paper` differs for print-a4). `any` needs one (`format` matches for any-a4). pdf-only lists just `format`, so `all` is satisfied.

steps.title: Nowhere to go: unroutable messages
body: If no binding matches, a message is **silently dropped**. Your publisher logs success, the broker even
confirms it, and the data is gone. Two fixes, often used together:
- **`mandatory: true`** on the publish: the broker sends an unroutable message **back** (`basic.return`).
In RabbitMQ.Client 7 with confirmation tracking on, `BasicPublishAsync` then throws a `PublishException`.
The publisher must decide what to do with it.
- An **alternate exchange** (AE) on the exchange: anything the exchange cannot route goes to the AE instead,
usually a fanout into an `orders.unrouted` queue you alert on. The publisher is not told.
```csharp
await channel.ExchangeDeclareAsync("orders.unrouted", ExchangeType.Fanout, durable: true);
await channel.QueueDeclareAsync("orders.unrouted", durable: true, exclusive: false, autoDelete: false);
await channel.QueueBindAsync("orders.unrouted", "orders.unrouted", routingKey: "");
await channel.ExchangeDeclareAsync("orders", ExchangeType.Topic, durable: true,
arguments: new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["alternate-exchange"] = "orders.unrouted" });
Or as a policy, which you can change without redeclaring:
`rabbitmqctl set_policy AE "^orders$" '{"alternate-exchange":"orders.unrouted"}' --apply-to exchanges`.
If the AE routes the message, it counts as routed and `mandatory` returns nothing. If the AE itself does not
exist, the message is dropped.
> **See it:** **Labs → Messaging builder → RabbitMQ**, challenge *Nowhere to go*.

prompt: **Symptom first.** Since the routing refactor, the billing queue stays empty. The publisher sends
`order.eu.created` and logs no errors; the audit queue receives every order. What is wrong?
options: The binding key `order.created.*` has its words in the wrong order: it matches `order.created.eu`, not `order.eu.created`. Bind `order.*.created` and remove the old binding.
Topic bindings need `#` instead of `*`: change it to `order.created.#`.
billing is also bound to the default exchange (first row), which steals its messages.
audit's `order.#` binding consumes the message first, so billing cannot get it.
explain: Every matching queue gets its own copy, so audit takes nothing from billing. The first row is the default
exchange's automatic binding and is harmless. Fix it with `QueueBindAsync("billing", "orders", "order.*.created")`
and `QueueUnbindAsync("billing", "orders", "order.created.*")`. Then add `mandatory: true` or an alternate
exchange, so the next silent drop is loud.

steps.prompt: Match the publisher setup to what happens to an unroutable message.
pairs: Routed to the alternate exchange; the publisher is not told
Confirmed with an ack: unroutable is not a confirm failure
steps.explain: Confirms answer "did the broker take responsibility?", not "did it reach a queue?". Only mandatory or an AE catches routing mistakes.

steps.title: A router over bindings with an alternate exchange
prompt: Write a class `Router` that models exchanges, bindings and unroutable messages:
- `void DeclareExchange(string name, string type, string? alternateExchange = null)`: `type` is `"direct"`,
`"topic"` or `"fanout"`; anything else throws `ArgumentException`.
- `void Bind(string exchange, string queue, string bindingKey)`: an undeclared exchange throws
`InvalidOperationException`.
- `List<string> Publish(string exchange, string routingKey, bool mandatory = false)`: returns the queues that get
a copy, **distinct and sorted** (ordinal). Publishing to an undeclared exchange throws
`InvalidOperationException` (the broker's `NOT_FOUND`).
- If nothing matches and the exchange has an alternate exchange **that exists**, route the same message
through it (an AE may have its own AE; never visit an exchange twice).
- If it is still unroutable and `mandatory` is set, add `"{exchange} {routingKey}"` to `Returned`.
- `List<string> Returned` (get-only): what came back with `basic.return`.
Topic bindings use the `*` / `#` rules from the matcher you just wrote (copy it into the class as a private helper).

Loop: match on the current exchange; if empty, move to its AE unless it is null, missing or already visited.
Only after the loop gives nothing: `if (mandatory) Returned.Add(...)`.

Dojo.Eq("topic: only audit", new List<string> { "audit" }, dojoR.Publish("orders", "order.refunded"));
Dojo.Eq("unroutable goes to the alternate exchange", new List<string> { "unrouted" }, dojoR.Publish("orders", "refund.eu", mandatory: true));

Dojo.Eq("direct exact match", new List<string> { "old-billing" }, dojoR.Publish("legacy", "invoice"));
Dojo.Eq("no AE, mandatory: nothing routed", new List<string>(), dojoR.Publish("legacy", "receipt", mandatory: true));
